# Consolidation external benchmark protocol

Status: design fixed; source freeze and scored execution pending. No scored solver has been run for this consolidation campaign.

The acceptance experiment is the complete recovered external suite: all46 available historical tasks and all9 later external extension tasks. Every one is labelled **exposed_regression**, because prior solver outcomes are known. They remain available for development/regression checks. Two historically unavailable selector slots remain visible, not solver failures. No synthetic input contributes to performance totals.

A separate prospective external evaluation cohort is fixed by HOLDOUT_FREEZE.json. Candidate metadata comes from the official UAI2022 MAR archives. The selection excludes every raw/canonical model hash found in available DGP review records (the recovered local packets cover DGP1–5 and DGP10; the earlier external packet adds the executed55 input bindings) and the prior55 executed inputs, then selects the minimum fixed salted task hash in each remaining family. This limits the claim to **not previously scored or used for development in available records**; inaccessible historical records prevent an absolute never-seen assertion. Inputs belong to known source families. Family membership is not a solver dispatch feature. The benchmark preparation agent keeps chosen names and contents from the implementation agent until the engine source is frozen. No solver outcomes are read to select them.

Exactly three primary arms run from a single frozen source/build identity: the new public `python -m pgm` automatic API, official libDAI0.3.2 junction tree (SUMPROD/HUGIN) and libDAI loopy BP (SEQMAX,1e-9 tolerance,10,000iteration limit). Two fresh-process replicates run serially, with reversed arm order in repeat2. All queried marginals refer to original nonobserved variables under the identical evidence. libDAI additionally serializes trivial observed point masses.

Each cell receives20 seconds end to end and3 GiB sampled process-tree RSS. PGM receives19.5 seconds internally; BP receives19 seconds. The supervisor has zero grace and10ms sampling. All parsing, imports, structural recognition, construction, abandoned attempts, inference, original-coordinate recovery, serialization and process cleanup count. Compilation and dependency installation are separate setup. The public API selects every route without benchmark-name rules, per-instance settings or hindsight arm choice. Epsilon is1/200 and request-level PAC delta is1/1,000,000. Python and numerical library threads are fixed to1.

The scored ceiling is8,000 supervisor seconds across both cohorts. The exposed suite runs first, then prospective evaluation without source, policy or harness changes between phases. Freeze is permitted only after source is committed; checked host native binaries/build records may differ from repository macOS binaries and are hashed explicitly. Every cell rechecks source, input and comparator identity before and after execution. All receipts, refusals, invalid outputs and timeouts remain in the record. A change after outcomes requires a new declared experiment; it cannot overwrite this one.

A task completes only if both repeats return every requested coordinate within the wall contract and pass independent original-inventory, input-binding, positive-mass, interval geometry and guarantee-label checks. Missing data from a killed worker is a failure, not an invented completion. Deterministic and PAC guarantees remain distinguished. libDAI supplies point outputs from binary64 arithmetic; BP convergence is not an epsilon certificate. JT serialization comparisons use a separately stated5e-10 allowance, never to loosen PGM certificate geometry. The driver drops positive scalar factors in logZ, so comparator logZ is not used as a certified original-model normalizer.

Report historical46, external9 and prospective evaluation separately. Report completion sets, one-repeat outcomes, all paired latency ratios and memory outcomes, plus raw failure classes. No memory refusal supplies a speedup denominator. A timeout yields only a censored lower bound. Exact-route and approximate-route guarantees remain visible. Prior accepted-engine, research-planner and legacy-dispatch results are retained as historical coverage references, not silently treated as same-round timing arms or combined into an imaginary selector.

Synthetic exact-oracle and adversarial fixtures are correctness tests only. Broad scaling/dominance is the program's target; this first integration experiment must not turn a selected holdout cohort or a median over mutually successful tasks into a universal scaling claim. A later larger external suite can extend the frozen benchmark without replacing these losses.

## Repository execution

The committed harness lives in `benchmarks/external/`, with its input manifests and all 61 model/evidence pairs. Runs are written under the ignored `benchmark_runs/` directory or an explicit `PGM_BENCH_RUN_DIR`; no original workstation paths or private records are needed. `PGM_BENCH_PY` selects the interpreter, and `PGM_LIBDAI` selects the qualified comparator. Native build identities include the four tracked host overlays, the active heat-bath build record/library, and the active contraction/stream cache copies. `CC` is explicitly bound at freeze; `CXX` follows the checked contraction build record. Read `README.md` for the executable commands.
